kwargs.profile_path: required: the profile directory (audit_surface passes profile['path'], as for write_settings). Everything else is read by the module itself from <profile_path>/config.yaml (approvals.*, terminal.backend, plugins.enabled / plugins.disabled, agent.disabled_toolsets, platform_toolsets, platforms, a2a_agents, mcp_servers, hooks, cron.*, security.*, ...) and from plugins/, hooks/, cron/ under it; no credential file is opened.
kwargs.managed_dir: optional, default None: same rule as write_settings._has_managed_overlay (HERMES_MANAGED_DIR, else /etc/hermes; skipped under pytest). Do not pass it unless the caller already passes it to write_settings.
kwargs.now_fn: optional, default time.monotonic; only bounds the 5 s budget and feeds run_metrics.elapsed_ms. Do not pass in production.
kwargs.max_entries / max_file_bytes / max_total: optional test-only caps (defaults MAX_ENTRIES=2000, MAX_CONFIG_BYTES, 8 MiB, 5.0 s). Do not pass in production.

vocabulary: An enabled user plugin declares pre_llm_call or pre_gateway_dispatch in its manifest and plugins/.install-metadata.json records it as installed without a pinned commit, so a plugin update can change the code that adds context to or rewrites user messages; this audit read the manifest and install metadata, did not load the plugin, and does not show what it added.

Approval-related settings in config.yaml differ from at least one config.yaml.bak copy in the profile folder; the copies hold earlier saved values, not when each value was active, and this audit did not check what ran under them.

Config keeps approvals.mode at smart and names an auxiliary.approval.model whose name carries a smaller-tier label; in smart mode that model answers APPROVE, DENY or ESCALATE for flagged commands and an APPROVE runs the command without asking a person; this audit read the model name only and did not measure the model's decisions.

Config lists, for one or more non-CLI platforms, toolsets that resolve to terminal, code_execution, cronjob or computer_use beyond that platform's shipped default, so sessions arriving on that platform can call those tools while it is connected; this audit read platform_toolsets and did not check whether the platform is connected or whether any remote session called the tools.

Config sets browser.use_real_profile to true, so local browser sessions run on a copy of the user's default Chromium-family browser profile, including its cookies and logins, whenever that profile can be copied; this audit read config settings and does not show which sites any browser session opened.

Config turns off a Hermes safety check that is on by default (protected instruction files, the unattended tool-loop hard stop) or turns on private-network URLs, so that check no longer stops the matching action; this audit read config settings and does not show that such an action happened.

Cron usage, output or execution records, or another job's context_from, name job IDs that cron/jobs.json does not contain; this audit read cron metadata and does not show what those jobs did or why they are absent.

One or more cron jobs in cron/jobs.json have a failure_streak of at least 5, the counter Hermes raises after each consecutive failed run and resets on success; this audit read job metadata and did not read job output.

One or more cron jobs in cron/jobs.json name a script or monitor_script, which the scheduler runs when the job fires; this audit read job definitions and does not show when the scripts ran or what they did.

One or more enumerated config keys hold a URL in a provider-name field or have leading or trailing whitespace; this audit read config syntax only and did not check how Hermes resolves these values, some of which its readers strip.

One or more unattended exposure settings, plugin manifests, hook entries, or cron records could not be verified from bounded static files; unverified items are not treated as clean or as enabled exposure.

config.yaml sets approvals.cron_mode, approvals.unattended_mode or approvals.single_query_mode to approve, so in cron jobs, on unattended platforms (webhook, msgraph_webhook, api_server) or in single-query runs Hermes runs commands and code that match its dangerous-command checks without asking a person (hardline blocks, the runtime self-delete and sudo stdin guards, and approvals.deny rules still apply); this audit read config settings and does not show what commands any agent ran.

config.yaml sets approvals.mode to off and terminal.backend to local, so Hermes runs shell commands that match its dangerous-command patterns on this machine without asking a person (hardline blocks and approvals.deny rules still apply); this audit read config settings and does not show what commands any agent ran.
static inspection only; not runtime safety

free_strings.what: absolute path of an existing plugin directory (<profile>/plugins/<dir> or <profile>/plugins/<category>/<dir>) whose manifest declares hooks; replaces the manifest name and version
free_strings.why_safe: an existing directory inside the audited home at most two levels below plugins/; the serializer keeps it unchanged (resolve + lstat); never a credential-named path (credential-named entries are skipped before any read)

free_strings.what: absolute path of an existing enabled plugin directory that has no readable manifest (status empty_dir / missing_manifest / portable_manifest_not_read); null for status symlink_skipped, because the serializer would resolve the link to its target outside the home
absolute path of a regular (non-symlink) file directly in <profile>/hooks/ whose name matches ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$; null otherwise
free_strings.why_safe: existing regular file one level below the profile; credential-named files are skipped; only the first line (<=256 bytes) is read, for the interpreter class

notes: Call shape: _component('unattended_exposure', identity, unattended_exposure.audit_unattended_exposure, profile_path=profile['path']); then section = res.get('unattended_exposure', <not_measured section>) and add 'unattended_exposure' to the measurements tuple in store.finalize_run (store.py:1144). The section name itself is listed in schema_keys.

Envelope keys are exactly unattended_exposure, findings, run_metrics, status, coverage. adapt_component_result (contract.py:570-618) copies every key other than ok/status/error/findings/coverage/classification verbatim, so run_metrics AND unattended_exposure survive unchanged; status ('pass' from make_component_envelope, never 'error') is kept only as legacy_status_ignored; coverage is re-derived (could_not_verify whenever a could_not_verify finding exists). run_metrics = {'elapsed_ms': int} is wall-clock dependent: store it outside the fingerprinted report (do not put it in measurements).

Digest safety: the section has no wall-clock field (test_section_and_findings_identical_with_clocks_days_apart). truncated_by='time_budget' can still appear when the 5 s budget is hit; that is a coverage fact, same as other caps.

Free strings: the section and findings emit no string the serializer would tokenise. Plugin names/versions were replaced by the plugin directory's absolute path plus version_declared; enabled-but-unloadable plugins by their directory's absolute path (null for symlinks); hook file names by the file's absolute path (null for names outside the safe pattern); cron ghost job ids by ghost_jobs_count only; unknown platform keys (formerly other_<n> dict keys) by the list platform_toolsets.other_platforms (rows without names); memory_provider_plugins by memory_provider_count. Emitted paths are built from profile_path.resolve() so EvidenceSerializer.scalar (evidence.py:236-250: resolve + lstat) returns them unchanged; they must exist when the report is serialized (same run). Tests: test_two_runs_give_identical_sealed_section_and_findings and _hmac_spots == [] in the sealing and canary tests.

Finding evidence is scalar-only (numbers, booleans, vocabulary strings) because persistence.finding_dto (persistence.py:177-202) drops every list and every string outside _EVIDENCE_VOCAB_KEYS; per-item lists live in the section (platform_toolsets.non_cli_platforms, plugins.hook_plugins via evidence.hook_plugin_index, config_backup_drift.approval_changed_keys, config_sanity.*_keys). 'value' (guardrail_disabled) is a boolean and is listed in numeric_evidence_keys; 'source' and 'reason' are already in _EVIDENCE_VOCAB_KEYS.

evidence_vocabulary SCHEMA_KEYS must include the dotted setting keys (approvals.mode, ...) because settings and config_backup_drift.changes use them as dict keys; they are also VOCABULARY values (changed_keys, guard, provider_url_keys, whitespace_value_keys).

Finding limitations is the existing sealed label 'static inspection only; not runtime safety' (already in CODE_LABELS); affected_identities/source path values are 'config.yaml', 'plugins', 'cron', 'cron/jobs.json' and '.' (the last four are not in VOCABULARY today and are listed in vocabulary).
